results.label: Quarterbacks taken in a first round

target.source: Pro Football Reference's draft pages, 2015 to 2024: 35 quarterbacks in 10 first rounds, from 1 in 2022 to 6 in 2024 (2, 3, 3, 5, 3, 4, 5, 1, 3, and 6).
target.note: Every draft the chained leagues held; round 1 without its compensatory picks' later placement, as the NFL counts it.

results.label: Median cap space at week 1, share of the cap

target.source: Over the Cap's team cap space as Pro Football Rumors listed it: on June 2, 2025, a median of $24.2M against the $279.2M cap (8.7%), quartiles of 6.0% and 11.4%, and New England's $67.3M (24.1%) the most; on October 27, 2024, a median of $8.6M against $255.4M (3.4%), quartiles of 1.8% and 7.5%, and San Francisco's $54.1M (21.2%) the most.
target.note: Week 1 cap sheets: each team's space under the cap, carryover included as Over the Cap counts it, as a share of the cap; the mean of each season's median. Week 1 falls between June's space and October's, after camp's extensions and before the season's signings.

results.label: Most cap space at week 1, share of the cap

target.source: Over the Cap's team cap space as Pro Football Rumors listed it: on June 2, 2025, a median of $24.2M against the $279.2M cap (8.7%), quartiles of 6.0% and 11.4%, and New England's $67.3M (24.1%) the most; on October 27, 2024, a median of $8.6M against $255.4M (3.4%), quartiles of 1.8% and 7.5%, and San Francisco's $54.1M (21.2%) the most.
target.note: The mean of each season's largest week 1 space, as a share of the cap.

results.label: Teams over the cap at week 1, per season

target.source: The CBA's Article 13 (Over the Cap's copy): every club must be under the cap at all times during the league year.
target.note: Teams over the cap on their week 1 cap sheets, per season.

results.label: Dead money at week 1, share of the caps

target.source: Pro Football Rumors' dead money by team: $798M league-wide on July 14, 2023, 11.1% of 32 caps of $224.8M; $1,456M on November 27, 2024 (Over the Cap's figures), 17.8% of 32 caps of $255.4M.
target.note: Dead money on the week 1 cap sheets (proration and money owed from deals that ended), as a share of the league's caps. Summer's figures run below the fall's, which add in-season releases.

results.label: Richest quarterback deal's yearly value, share of the cap

target.source: The richest quarterback deals by yearly value as each season opened: Joe Burrow's $55M (September 2023), 24.5% of the $224.8M cap; Dak Prescott's $60M (September 2024), 23.5% of $255.4M, still the richest in 2025 at 21.5% of $279.2M. The market curve's top for quarterbacks (tuning market) is that record against the cap it was signed under, 23.5% (D-65), and the richest deal's share falls between new records as the cap grows.
target.note: The largest yearly value of a quarterback's deal on week 1, as a share of the cap; the mean over seasons.

results.label: Richest deal apart from quarterbacks', share of the cap

target.source: The richest deals apart from quarterbacks: Nick Bosa's $34M (September 2023), 15.1% of the $224.8M cap; Justin Jefferson's $35M (June 2024), 13.7% of $255.4M; Micah Parsons's $47M (August 2025, NFL.com), 16.8% of $279.2M.
target.note: The largest yearly value of any other player's deal on week 1, as a share of the cap; the mean over seasons.

results.label: Unrestricted free agents who signed with a new team, per team
Richest of their deals' yearly value, share of the cap

target.source: The richest deals unrestricted free agents signed with new teams: Kirk Cousins's $45M a year with Atlanta (March 2024), 17.6% of the $255.4M cap; Sam Darnold's $33.5M a year with Seattle (March 2025), 12.0% of $279.2M.
target.note: Among the unrestricted free agents whose deals ran out as the league year opened and who signed with a new team, the largest yearly value by week 1, as a share of the cap; the mean over seasons.

results.label: New veteran deals' yearly value over the market price, median

target.source: The market curve (tuning market) prices each position, rating, and age from the 2026 market, its tops the richest deals at each position against the $301.2M cap; D-60 has the money new deals settle for center on it.
target.note: Veteran deals that start the league year (re-signings, extensions, and free agents), for players rated 70 or more, read as the OTAs end: each one's yearly value over the market price for the player when he signed (his rating before camp's development, his age that day), the median over every judged season's deals. Rookie deals, tags, tenders, and the practice squad don't count.

results.label: The same for free agents who changed teams

target.source: The market curve (tuning market) and D-60, as for new deals: free agents who change teams sign at the market's price or over it, where teams with room compete for them (D-60's room premium).
target.note: The median of the same ratio for the unrestricted free agents who signed with a new team.

results.label: Widest gap between position groups' medians

target.source: The market curve (tuning market) prices every position against its own top, so each position group's new deals should center on it about alike.
target.note: The widest gap between position groups' median ratios, counting groups with 20 deals or more.

results.label: Movers' first-week deals over their later ones, medians

target.source: Spec 11.8: top players sign early and the market softens for those who wait; the user's M12 additions ask that free agency's prices run highest in its first days and fall as the market settles (D-65). A direction check, since no public count prices free agents' deals against their value by the week they signed.
target.note: Free agents who changed teams: the median first-week deal's yearly value over the market price when he signed, over the same median for the later weeks' deals.

results.label: Compensatory picks for net losses, per draft

target.source: NFL.com, "2025 NFL Draft: NFL awards 35 compensatory picks": 32 awarded under the net loss formula, and 3 special picks for minority coaching and executive hires; Over the Cap's methodology: net value and supplemental picks fill the 32 only when the formula falls short.
target.note: Compensatory picks for net losses of qualifying free agents, per draft, before net value and supplemental picks fill the 32 (D-58).

results.label: Cash paid in a league year, share of the cap

target.source: Over the Cap, "CBA Suggestion Number 4" (April 2019): from 2015 to 2018 the league's average cash spending was about 101% of the cap; the CBA's league-wide minimum is 95% over each four-year period.
target.note: Cash each team paid in a league year (salary for the weeks in force, bonuses when paid, money owed after releases), as a share of that year's cap, across the league, from each chain's second salary floor window: the generated league's deals carry bonuses paid before it began, which charge its first seasons' caps with no cash.

results.label: Lowest team's cash over a floor window, share of its caps

target.source: Over the Cap, "CBA Suggestion Number 4" (April 2019): the lowest-spending team from 2015 to 2018, Houston, paid 92.8% of the cap; the club minimum is 89% (D-33).
target.note: The lowest team's cash over each four-year salary floor window, as a share of the window's caps; windows from each chain's second, since the first holds the generated league's deals.

results.label: Teams short of the salary floor, per window

target.source: Over the Cap, "CBA Suggestion Number 4" (April 2019): no team came close to the 89% club minimum from 2015 to 2018.
target.note: Teams short of the salary floor per four-year window (D-33), windows from each chain's second.
